The Blue Grain in the Burial Bowl

墓葬陶碗上的蓝色颗粒 · 648 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A museum received a clay bowl from an ancient burial site. Its label linked it to a temple and described its blue grains as a rare mineral. A historian named Leila saw a familiar piece of tin beneath the rim. It looked too even to be primitive. The bowl might preserve evidence of trade, religious practice, or a modern repair. Before a donor paid for a display on an early civilization, Leila asked whether they could trace the grain to its origin.

2Excavation records showed a chamber beneath volcanic rock. A skeleton lay by a statue, ash, and a broken sword. The bony remains made the site look like a grave, yet a superficial comparison linked it to a place of worship. An old catalogue mentioned a priest and a myth about a golden bowl. It gave no location for the settlement. Leila asked the archaeological bureau to treat the so-called temple as an uncertainty rather than assume every object came from the same tradition.

3A scientist examined a detached fragment. A cubic crystal sat in a milky layer above the clay. A chemist used a harmless light test to compare it with samples of coal, ore, and several metal compounds. One sample contained nickel and another left a silvery trace. None matched the grain. A shallow bubble at its edge was more informative. The grain had not formed inside the bowl. It appeared to have been pressed into a layer of repair material that hardened much later.

4Preservation notes were fragmentary. A repairer had acquired the bowl from a mining village near a coal mine. He kept its base in a cupboard with his toolbox. A church that wanted to teach local Christianity had paid him to repair a prayer vessel, a figure from a mosque, and several pieces of household ware. He did not label every alteration. Leila found his handwriting on a box of wood. The word "tin" referred to a support rather than to a precious mineral.

5The repairer described a powder that absorbed moisture. A small leak could carry it into the rim. Leila asked a chemist to investigate whether acid in the new layer had altered the older clay. One edge remained pure. Elsewhere a dark trace contained carbon, and a pale grain showed an unusual metallic peculiarity. The scientist mapped that fragmentation without cutting the bowl. The repair had value as part of the object's history even if the material itself was less of a rarity than the label implied.

6Another researcher wanted to use the bowl for a lesson on dating. A fossil or a diamond could give evidence about a vast period of geological change. A repair in clay belonged to a much shorter human story. The old label had confused the existence of an ancient settlement with the age of one peculiar grain. Leila offered a map and an approximate date. That was more useful than calling every mysterious fragment a treasure.

7A descendant of the village's founder lent them a photograph. Its landscape showed rooftops, the church, and a quarry that had closed after years of exploitation. The photographer also kept a card naming the craftsman's address. It offered a unique link between the museum's bowl and its repair. The museum could preserve local heritage and respect the uncertainty about ancient belief. Leila placed a plain image of the bowl beside the old excavation map.

8A visitor asked if the bowl was less precious. Leila showed him its repair beside the burial map. A local ancestor had put the vessel in the earth. A much later repairer left a grain from another century. The enlarged image seemed mysterious only when it stood alone. Leila did not call it a holy object or claim to know the extent of the ancient settlement. The bowl could help people explore its history without turning a similarity into proof of origin.

四级汇总词汇 · 24中文译文

墓葬陶碗上的蓝色颗粒

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1博物馆收到一只出自古墓的陶碗。标签把它和一座寺庙联系起来，称蓝色颗粒是一种罕见矿物。历史学者莱拉在碗沿下看见一小片熟悉的锡，太规整了，不像早期工艺。碗可能留下贸易、宗教活动或现代修补的证据。捐赠人还没为古文明展付钱，莱拉先问能不能追到蓝粒的来源。

2发掘记录显示，火山岩下面有个空间。骨骼旁是雕像、灰烬和一把断剑。骨头让现场看上去像坟墓，粗略比较却把它与礼拜场所联系起来。旧目录提到一位祭司和金碗的传说，没写聚居点在哪里。莱拉请考古部门把所谓寺庙视作尚未确定的说法，别先假定所有物件都出自同一传统。

3科学家检查一块脱落的碎片。陶土上方的乳白层有一粒立方晶体。化学人员用无害的光照测试，与煤、矿石和几种金属化合物作对照。一份样品含镍，另一份留下银色痕迹，都对不上。颗粒边缘的小气泡更有用。它没有在碗内自然形成，像是后来有人把它压进一层修补材料，等材料再硬化。

4保存记录零零碎碎。修理匠从煤矿旁的矿村买到碗，把底座和工具箱放在柜子里。一家教堂想传播当地的基督教传统，付钱请他修祈祷用的器皿、清真寺里的一件人像和一些家用器物。他没有给每一处改动写标签。莱拉在木盒上认出他的笔迹。上面的“锡”指一个小支撑物，并非珍贵矿物。

5修理匠提到一种吸潮粉末，有小缝就可能渗进碗沿。莱拉请化学人员看看，新涂层里的酸有没有改变旧陶土。一边仍是纯陶土，别处的黑痕含碳，浅色颗粒则显示特别的金属特征。科学家不切开碗，也能把破碎处画出来。即便材料没有标签暗示的那么稀有，修补本身也成了器物历史的一部分。

6另一位研究人员想拿这只碗讲年代测定。化石或钻石能给出漫长地质时期的线索，陶土上的修补则属于短得多的人类故事。旧标签把一个古聚落确曾存在，和一粒特别的蓝色颗粒有多老混为一谈。莱拉给出地图和大概年代，比把每块神秘碎片都叫宝物更有帮助。

7村庄创办人的后代借给他们一张照片。画面里有屋顶、教堂，以及多年开采后关闭的采石场。摄影师还留了一张写有工匠地址的卡片，让博物馆的碗和这次维修有了具体联系。博物馆可以保留当地遗产，也可以如实承认对古老信仰所知有限。莱拉把朴素的碗照放在旧发掘图旁。

8访客问碗是不是没原来那么珍贵。莱拉让他把修补处和墓葬图一起看。当地先人把容器埋在地下，许多年后，修理匠又留下了一粒蓝色颗粒。放大的图单独看才显得神秘。莱拉没把它叫作圣物，也没声称知道古聚落有多大。碗能让人了解它自己的来历，相似之处还不足以证明它出自哪里。
